title: Fair Scales, and Abraham Breaks the Idols

paragraphs.text: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will set up fair scales, and no soul will be wronged at all. Even a deed as small as a mustard seed will be brought forward. Allah gave Moses and Aaron the criterion, a light and a reminder for the righteous. They fear their Lord unseen and fear the Hour. This Qur'an is also a blessed reminder. Will they deny it?

Allah gave Abraham good judgement before. He asked his father and people, "What are these statues you are devoted to?" They said their fathers worshipped them. He said they and their fathers were clearly wrong. They asked if he was serious or joking. He said, "Your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and earth, who created them, and I am a witness to this."

He swore by Allah to plan against their idols. When they left, he broke them into pieces, except the biggest one, so they might return to it. The people asked who had done this. Some said they heard a young man named Abraham speak about them. They brought him before everyone. They asked, "Did you do this to our gods?" He said, "No, this biggest one did it. Ask them, if they can speak."

hardWords.m: a tool used to weigh things
a plant with very tiny seeds
something that shows right from wrong
